metadata.name: Benign prostatic enlargement with lower urinary tract symptoms
metadata.name_ar: تضخم البروستاتا الحميد مع أعراض المسالك البولية السفلية
metadata.organ_system: Prostate, bladder outlet and lower urinary tract
metadata.emergency_level: Usually routine; emergency with acute retention, renal compromise, sepsis or severe haematuria
metadata.severity: Chronic quality-of-life condition with potentially serious retention/renal complications

overview.short_description: Non-malignant prostate enlargement that may contribute to bothersome voiding and storage urinary symptoms in adults with a prostate.
overview.detailed_description: Male LUTS are not synonymous with BPH: infection, medicines, overactive/underactive bladder, neurological disease, stricture and prostate/bladder cancer must be considered. Initial assessment measures symptom impact and detects retention, renal or cancer red flags before conservative, drug or surgical treatment.
overview.pathophysiology: Prostatic stromal/epithelial enlargement and smooth-muscle tone can increase bladder-outlet resistance; bladder compensation and later dysfunction create mixed voiding, storage and post-micturition symptoms.
overview.etiology: Age-related androgen-dependent prostate growth interacting with bladder and neurological factors.
overview.natural_history: Usually gradual; symptoms and prostate size correlate imperfectly. Some remain stable while others develop retention, infection, stones or renal effects.
overview.prognosis: Usually manageable; progression risk varies by enlargement, symptoms and complications.

prevalence.value: Common with increasing age in people with a prostate

mortality.value: Not usually fatal; complications and missed cancer are the key risks

risk_factors.obesity: Metabolic factors may associate with LUTS
risk_factors.medications: Decongestants, anticholinergics, opioids, diuretics and others may worsen symptoms/retention
risk_factors.previous_diseases: Diabetes, neurological disease, UTI, stones, urethral stricture or prior pelvic/prostate procedures

chief_complaints.importance: Storage LUTS; not specific to BPH

symptoms.symptom: Inability to pass urine with painful bladder

negative_findings.why_important: BPH histology/enlargement alone does not require symptom treatment
Does not exclude functional LUTS or modest enlargement

negative_findings.finding: No retention, infection, haematuria, renal impairment or cancer features

history_questions.question: Which symptoms: weak stream/hesitancy, urgency/frequency, nocturia or dribbling, and how much do they bother you?
Any complete retention, recurrent infection, visible blood, fever or flank pain?
Any weight loss, bone pain, abnormal prostate history or family cancer risk?
Review all medicines, fluids, caffeine/alcohol, constipation and sleep-apnoea/diabetes/heart-failure symptoms?
Any dizziness/falls, cataract surgery, sexual/fertility priorities or cognitive/constipation issues?

physical_examination.examination: External genital and digital rectal examination when appropriate
physical_examination.expected_finding: Assess prostate and alternative genital causes; suspicious abnormality changes pathway
Baseline before alpha blocker; detect postural hypotension

vital_signs.heart_rate: Usually normal; tachycardia may indicate pain, dehydration or sepsis
vital_signs.blood_pressure: Include postural measurement when considering alpha blocker
vital_signs.respiratory_rate: Usually normal; elevation may indicate sepsis/pain
vital_signs.bmi: Record when relevant to risk or treatment

laboratory_tests.expected_result: Detect blood, glucose, protein or infection
laboratory_tests.normal_range: Use current local laboratory reference range

laboratory_tests.indication: When renal impairment is suspected, such as palpable bladder, enuresis, recurrent UTI or stone history
laboratory_tests.normal_range: Use current local laboratory reference range

laboratory_tests.test_name: PSA after informed discussion when indicated
laboratory_tests.indication: Cancer concern, abnormal prostate or symptoms suggesting outlet obstruction/BPE
laboratory_tests.expected_result: Interpret by age/context and before/with 5-ARI effects
laboratory_tests.normal_range: Use current local laboratory reference range

imaging.when_needed: Not routine in uncomplicated initial assessment; use in specialist/retention/renal/stone/recurrent-infection pathways
imaging.expected_findings: Prostate size, residual urine, hydronephrosis, bladder/stone findings

ecg.when_needed: Not routine; use when cardiac disease, electrolyte disturbance or medicine risk indicates

other_diagnostic_tests.biopsy: Not a BPH test; prostate-cancer pathway only when indicated

diagnostic_criteria.formal_criteria: Bothersome LUTS assessed by history and examination, with plausible benign prostatic/bladder-outlet contribution after considering infection, medicines, neurological/bladder disease and cancer. IPSS quantifies symptoms but does not prove BPH.

diagnostic_scores.value: Use a validated symptom score such as IPSS before treatment and for follow-up.

diagnostic_criteria.cutoff_values: Use current guideline criteria for prostate size/PSA and retention; do not treat a copied cutoff without context.

differential_diagnosis.differences: Abnormal prostate, visible haematuria, weight loss or bone pain
differential_diagnosis.distinguishing_symptoms: Abnormal prostate, visible haematuria, weight loss or bone pain
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Any blood, weight loss or bone pain?
Any neurological symptoms or urgency leakage?

differential_diagnosis.differences: Trauma, instrumentation, STI or surgery history
differential_diagnosis.distinguishing_symptoms: Trauma, instrumentation, STI or surgery history

differential_diagnosis.differences: Back pain, saddle anaesthesia, leg weakness
differential_diagnosis.distinguishing_symptoms: Back pain, saddle anaesthesia, leg weakness
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Any new saddle numbness or leg weakness?

diagnostic_questions.question: Is there retention, recurrent UTI, suspected renal impairment or cancer concern?
Are symptoms mainly voiding or storage, and what is the IPSS impact?

next_best_question.question: Any retention, recurrent infection, haematuria/cancer features, renal concern, neurological red flags, and is the pattern voiding or storage?
next_best_question.expected_answers: Complicated versus uncomplicated and symptom subtype
next_best_question.branching_logic: Complication/red flag -> urgent/specialist; uncomplicated -> score, conservative care and matched medicine if needed

next_best_test.test: Urinalysis plus focused examination and symptom score

next_best_test.why: Avoid routine low-value testing while detecting renal/cancer/retention risk

red_flags.finding: Retention with renal impairment/hydronephrosis or anuria
Visible haematuria, abnormal hard/nodular prostate, weight loss or bone pain
Retention with saddle anaesthesia, leg weakness or severe back pain

referral_criteria.urgent_referral: Acute retention, renal impairment/hydronephrosis, recurrent/persistent UTI, significant haematuria or cancer concern.
referral_criteria.routine_referral: Bothersome LUTS unresponsive to conservative/drug treatment or diagnostic uncertainty.
referral_criteria.emergency_referral: Retention with sepsis, anuria/renal compromise or cauda equina features.

initial_management.supportive_care: Classify symptoms and complications, review medicines/lifestyle and use a symptom score.
initial_management.medications: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): Alpha blocker; 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor; Antimuscarinic; Beta-3 adrenoceptor agonist. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: NICE_CG97_2024.
initial_management.lifestyle_advice: Adjust fluid timing, caffeine/alcohol and constipation; bladder training when appropriate.
initial_management.follow_up: Review response and adverse effects at medicine-specific intervals; refer failure/complications.
initial_management.legacy_medications_pre_v13: Matched alpha blocker, 5-ARI or storage-symptom medicine only after contraindication and retention/cancer assessment.

patient_education.home_advice: An enlarged prostate is benign, but urinary symptoms can have other causes. Inability to pass urine, blood in urine, fever, severe back/leg neurological symptoms or worsening kidney function need urgent assessment.
patient_education.home_advice_ar: تضخم البروستاتا الحميد ليس سرطاناً، لكن أعراض البول قد تكون لها أسباب أخرى. عدم القدرة على التبول، أو وجود دم في البول، أو الحمى، أو أعراض عصبية شديدة في الظهر/الساقين، أو تدهور وظائف الكلى تحتاج تقييماً عاجلاً.
patient_education.prevention: No proven prevention; reduce aggravating factors and monitor progression/complications.
patient_education.warning_signs: Complete retention, haematuria, fever, flank pain, weakness/numbness or reduced urine.

prevention.lifestyle: Manage fluids/caffeine/alcohol, constipation and contributing medicines
prevention.screening: No BPH screening programme; evaluate symptoms and discuss PSA when indicated

evidence.evidence_level: Guideline-grounded direction; no claim that every narrative sentence has clinician verification.
evidence.guideline_strength: The main diagnosis/test and treatment direction was checked against the current guidance identified by NICE_CG97_2024; see evidence_review for scope and limitations. This does not verify every legacy narrative sentence.

The evidence audit verifies traceability and major safety structure; it does not certify every narrative sentence.
No medication should be selected or dosed without patient-specific contraindication and interaction checking.

treatment_guidance.treatment_goal: Relieve bothersome male lower-urinary-tract symptoms, identify retention/renal or cancer red flags and match treatment to symptom type and progression risk.
treatment_guidance.legacy_narrative_summary: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): Alpha blocker; 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor; Antimuscarinic; Beta-3 adrenoceptor agonist. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: NICE_CG97_2024.
required_history_before_any_medication: age and weight where dosing is weight- or age-dependent
pregnancy or breastfeeding status when relevant
documented drug allergies and the exact reaction
all prescribed, OTC, herbal and recreational substances
major cardiovascular, respiratory, gastrointestinal and bleeding history
non_drug_measures: Review fluid timing, caffeine/alcohol, constipation and contributing medicines; use bladder training for storage symptoms and a validated symptom score for baseline/follow-up.

medication_options.role: first-line medicine for moderate-severe voiding LUTS
medication_options.when_to_consider: After postural blood pressure, falls, cataract-surgery and interaction assessment
medication_options.dose_policy: Dose is not inferred from this KB; use age, weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status and the current local formulary/medicine label.

avoid_if: symptomatic severe hypotension or serious product reaction
use_caution_if: postural hypotension/syncope, falls, cataract surgery, PDE-5 inhibitor/other antihypertensive use, hepatic/renal impairment, or pregnancy when used off-label for stones
monitoring: blood pressure, dizziness/falls, symptom response and ejaculatory adverse effects; alert cataract surgeon

medication_options.when_to_consider: When prostate size/PSA and progression risk meet guideline criteria and delayed benefit is acceptable
medication_options.dose_policy: Dose is not inferred from this KB; use age, weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status and the current local formulary/medicine label.

avoid_if: pregnancy exposure to crushed/leaking product or serious product reaction
use_caution_if: liver disease, planned PSA interpretation, sexual/fertility concerns, depression history, or suspected prostate cancer
monitoring: symptoms and adverse effects; PSA must be interpreted in light of therapy; response is delayed and requires scheduled review

medication_options.when_to_consider: Overactive-bladder symptoms after retention/obstruction and cognitive/anticholinergic-risk review
medication_options.dose_policy: Dose is not inferred from this KB; use age, weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status and the current local formulary/medicine label.

avoid_if: urinary retention, gastric retention, uncontrolled narrow-angle glaucoma, or serious product reaction
use_caution_if: high post-void residual/obstruction, cognitive impairment, older/frail patient, constipation, autonomic neuropathy, QT risk, or anticholinergic burden
monitoring: voiding/retention, cognition, constipation, dry mouth, vision and symptom response

medication_options.when_to_consider: When a current technology-appraisal/local pathway supports it and antimuscarinic is unsuitable or ineffective
medication_options.dose_policy: Dose is not inferred from this KB; use age, weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status and the current local formulary/medicine label.

avoid_if: severe uncontrolled hypertension for mirabegron or serious product reaction
use_caution_if: hypertension, tachyarrhythmia/QT risk, urinary retention/obstruction, renal/hepatic impairment, pregnancy, or interacting CYP medicines depending on agent
monitoring: blood pressure, pulse, urinary retention and symptom response

medication_options.option_name: Catheterisation, TURP, HoLEP or other selected urological procedure
medication_options.medication_or_class: Catheterisation, TURP, HoLEP or other selected urological procedure
medication_options.when_to_consider: Acute retention, renal compromise, recurrent complications or failed/inappropriate conservative and drug treatment
medication_options.dose_policy: Dose is not inferred from this KB; use age, weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status and the current local formulary/medicine label.
medication_options.clinical_note: Procedure selection requires prostate anatomy, bleeding/anticoagulation, continence, sexual-function and anaesthetic assessment.

procedures_referral_and_escalation: Immediate catheter pathway for acute retention; specialist referral for recurrent/persistent UTI, retention, suspected LUTS-related renal impairment, haematuria/cancer concern, abnormal prostate examination or failed treatment.
